items.title: Finite-grid Brownian quadratic-variation error in L²

source.attribution: Samplinglib formalizes the exact finite-grid mean-square identity that precedes a quadratic-variation limit argument.

items.statement: For a real pre-Brownian process on a deterministic monotone finite grid, the expected square of the compensated sum of squared increments is twice the sum of the squared time-step lengths.
assumptions: B is a real pre-Brownian process with its Gaussian increment law and independent increments.
The grid is a deterministic monotone map from Fin (n+1) to nonnegative real time.
Repeated grid points and the empty grid are allowed; no strict positivity or usual filtration conditions are assumed.
The scalar dyadic mean-square consumer is formalized separately; predictable weights, vector cross-variation, stochastic integration, and Ito's formula remain outside this finite-grid result.

obligations.label: Prove the exact L² identity for the compensated squared-increment sum

bindings.boundary: This theorem proves only the exact identity on each finite deterministic monotone grid. Its scalar dyadic L² consumer is formalized separately; predictable weights, vector cross-variation, stochastic integration, Taylor localization, and Ito's formula remain outside this theorem.

assumption_deltas.source: The quadratic-variation calculation uses centered Gaussian increments and independence over disjoint deterministic time cells.
assumption_deltas.lean: The Lean theorem assumes IsPreBrownianReal and a monotone nonnegative-time grid, then proves the same finite-grid second-moment identity, including degenerate cells.
assumption_deltas.reason: The process law, deterministic-grid condition, and exact constant agree; allowing repeated times only includes zero-length cells.
